lines.say: {c1}Three terms. {c2}A geometric sequence. {c3}All depending on k. {q}It converges. Find k, and the sum to infinity.
Real Edexcel A-level question. {pz}Pause and try it!
{rem1}Quick reminder: geometric means you multiply by the same ratio, r, every time. {rat}So second over first equals third over second.
{cross}Cross-multiply, {sq}and the middle squared equals first times third.
{exL}Expand the left: one four four, minus seventy-two k, plus nine k squared. {exR}The right: three k squared, plus fifty-two k, plus sixty-four.
{col}Put it all on one side, {half}halve it, and there's the quadratic: three k squared, minus sixty-two k, plus forty, equals zero.
{fac}It factorises: three k minus two, times k minus twenty. {roots}So k is two thirds, or twenty.
{rem2}Now remember: a geometric series only converges if r is between minus one and one.
{k23}Two thirds gives six, ten, sixteen and two thirds. {r23}r is five thirds. Too big! {boom}It runs off to infinity.
{k20}Twenty gives sixty-four, minus forty-eight, thirty-six. {r20}r is minus three quarters. {ok}That works! {hop}Watch the running total bounce in.
{rem3}Sum to infinity is a over one minus r. {sub}Sixty-four over one plus three quarters, {ans}which is two hundred and fifty-six over seven.
{trap}Leave it as a fraction! Thirty-six point six won't get the mark.
